mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: GDP increases but SPX returns are negative in >40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: FEDFUNDS above 4.5% signals tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS >4.5% but SPX returns positive in >50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, labor market strength boosts S&P 500.
failure_condition: PAYEMS up and UNRATE down but SPX negative in >30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, rising HOUST signals housing growth, boosting S&P 500.
failure_condition: HOUST rises but SPX returns negative in >40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: INDPRO growth indicates increased production, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth but SPX negative in >40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: UNRATE below 4% signals low unemployment, boosting S&P 500 in 5 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE <4% but SPX negative in >50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: GDPC1 growth and FEDFUNDS decline stimulate economic growth, boosting S&P 500.
failure_condition: GDPC1 up and FEDFUNDS down but SPX negative in >30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During tightening, FEDFUNDS increases lead to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS up but SPX positive in >50% of cases.
